question: Distinguish between a composite supply and a mixed supply under GST, with an example of each.
sources: CGST Act, 2017 - section 8 tax liability on composite and mixed supplies

points.label: Composite supply
points.description: Two or more taxable supplies that are naturally bundled and supplied together in the ordinary course of business, one of which is the principal supply.

points.label: Tax on composite supply
points.description: A composite supply is taxed as a supply of the principal supply.

points.label: Mixed supply
points.description: Two or more individual supplies made together for a single price that are not naturally bundled.

points.label: Tax on mixed supply and examples
points.description: A mixed supply is taxed at the rate of the supply that attracts the highest rate. Examples: goods with transport and insurance (composite); a gift pack of sweets, chocolates and dry fruits (mixed).
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, section 8(b); illustrations to sections 2(30) and 2(74)
